What.coughing: Coughing or sneezing, and no hope of going quietly.
What.drowsy: On the verge of sleep. A Will roll every two hours spent still, or they drop off until woken.
What.drunk: Highly intoxicated. Shyness is two levels lighter, and Cowardice is resisted as well as ever.
What.euphoria: Nothing is worth worrying about, and nothing is done well.
What.nauseated: A HT roll after eating, a foul odour, a failed Fright Check or a stunning, and every hour in free fall. A failure means vomiting.
What.moderatePain: Moderate pain. A high pain threshold halves it; a low one doubles it.
What.severePain: Severe pain. A high pain threshold halves it; a low one doubles it.
What.terriblePain: Terrible pain. A high pain threshold halves it; a low one doubles it.
What.tipsy: Slightly intoxicated. Shyness is one level lighter, and Cowardice is resisted as well as ever.
What.agony: Conscious, and able to do nothing but scream. A point of fatigue a minute, and a torturer who can promise more of it gets +3.
What.choking: Unable to breathe or speak, and suffocating. A friend may try First Aid to clear the throat, two seconds an attempt.
What.daze: Conscious and upright, and able to do nothing. A blow, a slap or a shake brings them round next turn.
What.ecstasy: Incapacitated by pleasure. Neither pain threshold reaches it, and an offer to continue is worth +3 on any Influence roll.
What.hallucinating: A Will roll before every success roll: a moment’s disorientation at -2, a minute of hallucination at -5, or something the GM decides.
What.paralysis: No voluntary muscle answers. Conscious, and able to use anything that needs neither speech nor movement.
What.retching: Vomiting, and good for nothing that needs concentration. A point of fatigue at the end, and no benefit from a recent meal or medicine.
What.seizure: Limbs trembling, unable to speak or think clearly. 1d fatigue at the end of it.
What.unconsciousness: Knocked out, as surely as by a wound.
What.coma: Collapsed. One HT roll to wake after twelve hours, and a roll every twelve hours after that, any failure of which is death.
What.heartAttack: Cardiac arrest. Straight to -1×FP, and dead in HT/3 minutes without resuscitation.

Affliction.ImmuneToHeartAttack: {name} has no vitals to stop, and cannot have a heart attack

Note.AgonyDrain: Loses {fatigue} FP a minute while it lasts
Note.TortureBonus: Anyone who can threaten more of it gets +{bonus} to Interrogation and Intimidation
Note.EcstasyInfluence: Anyone offering more of it gets +{bonus} to Influence rolls
Note.AgonyFunctions: High Pain Threshold: able to act, at {penalty} to DX and IQ
Note.NauseaRoll: Roll HT {target} after eating, a foul smell, a failed Fright Check or being stunned
Note.Vomits: On a failure, vomits for {seconds} seconds — treat as Retching
Note.HallucinationRoll: Roll Will before each success roll: success {success} for {successFor}; failure {failure} for {failureFor}; critical failure freaks out for {freakOutFor}
Note.HeartAttackClock: Drops to -FP, and dies in {minutes} minutes unless resuscitated

Rules.Title: GURPS rules in play
Rules.MenuHint: Turn individual GURPS rules on or off for this world. A rule that is off behaves as though it had never been written — no penalty, no control, nothing to explain.
Rules.Intro: GURPS is written to be played at several depths. Everything here is optional detail; the spine — success rolls, damage, DR and the active defenses — is always in play.
Rules.NoneYet: No rules are registered in this group yet.

magic.Name: Magic
magic.Hint: The whole chapter: Magery, spells learned as skills, and a Magic tab on the sheet. Off, the campaign has no magic and the tab is not shown.

manaLevels.Name: Mana levels
manaLevels.Hint: The mana of the world or the scene decides who can cast and at what: -5 in low mana, none at all with no mana, and every failure critical in very high mana.

magicRituals.Name: Magic rituals
magicRituals.Hint: High skill takes energy off the cost and time off the casting; low skill demands a full ritual and doubles the time.

criticalSpellFailure.Name: Critical Spell Failure Table
criticalSpellFailure.Hint: A critical failure rolls on the table: a backfire, a wrong target, a stunned caster, a demon.

maintainingSpells.Name: Spells running
maintainingSpells.Hint: Every spell still up costs the next casting -1, and one being concentrated on -3.

spellDistraction.Name: Distraction and injury
spellDistraction.Hint: A caster who defends, is hurt or is knocked about while concentrating rolls Will-3 to keep the spell.

ruleOf16.Name: The Rule of 16
ruleOf16.Hint: A Resisted spell's effective skill against a living subject is capped at 16, or at the subject's resistance if that is higher.

magicItems.Name: Magic items and enchanting
magicItems.Hint: Enchantments on gear: Accuracy, Deflect, Fortify, Puissance and Power read into the sheet, spells cast from an item at its Power, and the enchanting roll itself.

feint.Name: Feint
feint.Hint: Fake an attack: your margin over the foe's roll comes off his defense against your next attack.

deceptiveAttack.Name: Deceptive Attack
deceptiveAttack.Hint: Trade two points of your own skill for one off the foe's defenses.

rapidStrike.Name: Rapid Strike
rapidStrike.Hint: A second attack in the time of one, both at -6.

retreat.Name: Retreating
retreat.Hint: Step back as you defend: +3 to Dodge, +1 to most parries and blocks.

rapidFire.Name: Rapid fire
rapidFire.Hint: Fire a burst: a bonus for the shots sent, and Recoil decides how many land.

opportunityFire.Name: Opportunity fire
opportunityFire.Hint: Cover ground with a ready weapon on a Wait, and pay for how much of it.

closeCombat.Name: Close combat
closeCombat.Hint: Sharing a hex: only a weapon that reaches close is any use there.

slams.Name: Slams
slams.Hint: Run into someone. Damage comes off how fast you were going.

evading.Name: Evading
evading.Hint: Get past someone without knocking them down, as a Quick Contest of DX.

hitLocations.Name: Hit locations
hitLocations.Hint: Aim at a part of the body, with its own to-hit penalty, DR and wounding.

knockback.Name: Knockback
knockback.Hint: A heavy blow throws the target back, and may knock them down.

criticalTables.Name: Critical hit and miss tables
criticalTables.Hint: A critical does something in particular rather than only being named.

explosions.Name: Explosions
explosions.Hint: Collateral damage falling off with distance, and fragmentation.

afflictions.Name: Afflictions
afflictions.Hint: Attacks resisted with an attribute roll rather than doing damage.

regularContests.Name: Regular Contests
regularContests.Hint: A drawn-out contest of repeated rolls, rather than one apiece.

frightChecks.Name: Fright Checks
frightChecks.Hint: A Will roll against horror, with the Fright Check Table for failures.

extraEffort.Name: Extra Effort
extraEffort.Hint: Spend fatigue to push a roll or a feat of strength beyond its usual limit.

physicalActivities.Name: Physical activities
physicalActivities.Hint: Climbing, jumping, swimming, running, throwing distance and lifting.

knockdown.Name: Knockdown and stunning
knockdown.Hint: A major wound, or a head or vitals hit, calls for a HT roll to stay upright.

bleeding.Name: Bleeding
bleeding.Hint: A wound keeps costing HP each minute until it is bound. The book marks this optional for the bookkeeping.

grappling.Name: Grappling
grappling.Hint: Take hold of a foe, then take them down, pin them, or choke them.

exposure.Name: Heat, cold, hunger and thirst
exposure.Hint: The weather and the rations wearing a party down, a point of fatigue at a time.

poison.Name: Poison
poison.Hint: Doses that keep working: a resistance roll and a cycle of damage at a time.

intoxication.Name: Drinking
intoxication.Hint: An hourly roll against the drink, sober to tipsy to drunk to the floor.

disease.Name: Illness and infection
disease.Hint: Catching something, and the wound that goes bad afterwards.

malfunctions.Name: Malfunctions
malfunctions.Hint: A gun that fails on a high attack roll, and what it takes to clear.

dualWeaponAttack.Name: Dual-Weapon Attacks
dualWeaponAttack.Hint: Strike with both hands on one Attack maneuver, at -4 and -8.

scatter.Name: Scatter
scatter.Hint: Where a missed grenade actually landed, and how far the fragments reach.

overpenetration.Name: Overpenetration
overpenetration.Hint: A shot that goes through cover, a shield or a person into whatever is behind.

dirtyTricks.Name: Dirty tricks
dirtyTricks.Hint: Sand or a drink in the face: a thrown weapon, and a Will roll not to flinch.

reactions.Name: Reaction and Influence rolls
reactions.Hint: What strangers make of you, and talking them round.

mountedCombat.Name: Mounted combat
mountedCombat.Hint: Fighting from the saddle: defenses capped by Riding, and staying on.

highSpeed.Name: High-speed movement
highSpeed.Hint: Going faster than you can stop: turning radius, and pushing the envelope.

study.Name: Improvement through study
study.Hint: Hours of study become character points in the skill studied: 200 with a teacher, 400 alone or on the job.

jobs.Name: Jobs and cost of living
jobs.Hint: Money on the sheet: a monthly job roll that pays or does not, and a month's cost of living at your Status.

aging.Name: Aging
aging.Hint: From 50, a series of four HT rolls a year, one per attribute; a failure costs a level of it.

socialBackground.Name: Languages and cultures
socialBackground.Hint: A Broken language is -3 and an Accented one -1 on Influence rolls, and an unfamiliar culture -3 on the same skills.

sleep.Name: Missed sleep
sleep.Hint: A day is sixteen hours; past it, a point of fatigue and another every four hours, and only sleep gives them back.

hiking.Name: Hiking
hiking.Hint: Ten miles a Move a day, by terrain and weather, at the fatigue of a battle an hour.

collisions.Name: Collisions
collisions.Hint: Being struck by something moving: its HP times its velocity, over a hundred, in dice.

electricity.Name: Electricity
electricity.Hint: A shock: a HT roll not to be stunned, or burning damage and a HT roll not to be knocked out.

fire.Name: Flame
fire.Hint: Seconds in a fire, and whether a blow of burning damage set the clothes alight.

radiation.Name: Radiation
radiation.Hint: Doses in rads that accumulate and slowly heal, with a HT roll against the table each time.

vehicles.Name: Vehicles
vehicles.Hint: Equipment with a stat line, and a control roll at its Handling that fails by its Stability Rating.

battleFatigue.Name: Battle fatigue
battleFatigue.Hint: A fight that runs past ten seconds costs everyone in it a point of fatigue when the tracker closes.

trampling.Name: Trampling
trampling.Hint: Somebody much larger walks over you: a melee attack a dodge is the only answer to.

swarms.Name: Swarms
swarms.Hint: A cloud of bats, bees or rats as one attacker: it hits automatically, and is fought off by the hit point.

legalityClass.Name: Legality Class
legalityClass.Hint: Every controlled item carries a class from 0 (banned) to 4 (open). With a Control Rating set for the campaign, the Gear tab says what carrying each piece here would take: registration, a license, or a uniform.

weaponQuality.Name: Weapon quality
weaponQuality.Hint: Cheap, good, fine and very fine (Characters pp. 274-279): a fine blade cuts a point deeper, a fine rifle is a point more accurate and jams a point later, a cheap weapon breaks sooner. Off, every weapon is as the table lists it.

minimumSt.Name: Minimum ST
minimumSt.Hint: A weapon that needs more ST than you have is -1 to skill per point you lack, and costs an extra FP at the end of a tiring fight (Characters p. 270).

weaponBreakage.Name: Weapons that break
weaponBreakage.Hint: Parrying something three times your weapon’s weight may snap it; a fumble may break it, unless it is one of the resistant kinds; a foe may strike at it. A damaged weapon rolls on the Broken Weapons table (Campaigns pp. 376, 400, 485).

reloading.Name: Shots and reloading
reloading.Hint: A weapon keeps count of what is in it: each shot fired comes off, and reloading takes the Ready maneuvers the Shots column lists. A crossbow stronger than its user takes longer, or a goat’s foot (Campaigns p. 373, Characters p. 270).

ammunitionTypes.Name: Ammunition
ammunitionTypes.Hint: Hollow-point, armour-piercing hard core and APDS rounds, bodkin points and silver change what a shot does, and what it costs (Characters pp. 276, 279).

bluntTrauma.Name: Blunt trauma
bluntTrauma.Hint: Flexible armour that stops a blow still bruises: 1 HP per 5 points of crushing or 10 of cutting, impaling or piercing, and none at all if a single point got through (Campaigns p. 379).

frontArmor.Name: Partial armour
frontArmor.Hint: A breastplate marked “F” protects against attacks from the front alone, and a great helm costs its wearer the corner of their eye (Characters pp. 282-283).

layeredArmor.Name: Layered armour
layeredArmor.Hint: Armour over armour adds both DR, but only over something flexible and concealable, and costs -1 to DX and DX-based skills anywhere but the head (Characters p. 286).

damageToShields.Name: Damage to shields
damageToShields.Hint: A shield that turned a blow by the width of its own Defense Bonus took that blow squarely, and may break. The book calls this bookkeeping in the name of realism, so it is off unless you want it (Campaigns p. 484).

equipmentModifiers.Name: Equipment modifiers
equipmentModifiers.Hint: The tools of a trade are worth something to the roll that uses them: nothing for basic gear, +1 for good, +2 for fine, TL/2 for the best there is, and a penalty for improvising or working bare-handed (Campaigns p. 345).

vehicleManeuvers.Name: Vehicle maneuvers
vehicleManeuvers.Hint: A vehicle moves on its operator’s turn: a Move or Move and Attack puts them in charge, and any other maneuver — or being stunned — leaves it plowing ahead on last turn’s course. Jumping out is a collision at the vehicle’s speed (Campaigns p. 467).

repairs.Name: Repairs and breakdowns
repairs.Hint: Mending a damaged thing is half an hour and a skill roll against its price, and gives back as many hit points as the roll beat its target by; a thing at zero needs spare parts first. Gear left in the sand or the damp rolls to keep working at all (Campaigns pp. 484-485).

cinematicExplosions.Name: Cinematic explosions
cinematicExplosions.Hint: A blast does no direct damage and throws no fragments. All it does is knock people about, at a token 1 HP a yard (Campaigns p. 417).

cinematicKnockback.Name: Cinematic knockback
cinematicKnockback.Hint: A bullet shoves a man as a club would, and anyone knocked back rolls against IQ at -1 a yard or is mentally stunned next turn (Campaigns p. 417).

fleshWounds.Name: Flesh wounds
fleshWounds.Hint: One unspent character point turns a wound into a scratch: all but 1 point of the damage is ignored. A character with nothing to spend goes into debt (Campaigns p. 417).

tvActionViolence.Name: TV action violence
tvActionViolence.Hint: A point of fatigue and the next turn convert a failed defense into a success. Not against a punch, a club or a thrown rock, unless it was aimed at the skull or neck (Campaigns p. 417).

bulletproofNudity.Name: Bulletproof nudity
bulletproofNudity.Hint: A good-looking character defends better the less they are wearing, and moves faster with nothing on at all (Campaigns p. 417).

cannonFodder.Name: Cannon fodder
cannonFodder.Hint: Minor NPCs fail every defense, never go all out, and drop the moment anything gets through their DR (Campaigns p. 417).

infiniteAmmunition.Name: Infinite ammunition
infiniteAmmunition.Hint: Heroes never run out of ammunition or power cells, and their weapons never malfunction (Campaigns p. 417).

meleeEtiquette.Name: Melee etiquette
meleeEtiquette.Hint: A hero fighting hand to hand is faced one at a time. The rest wait their turn (Campaigns p. 417).

CombatStyle.Name: Combat system
CombatStyle.Hint: Basic combat is abstract: everyone can reach everyone and nobody has a back. Tactical combat is fought on a hex map, where facing decides what you can defend against. Tactical needs a hex-gridded scene; on any other grid the table falls back to basic.

SkillOrder.Name: Skill order
SkillOrder.Hint: How the Skills tab lists skills: grouped by controlling attribute as the printed sheet does, or as one alphabetical list.

Facing.Name: Facing arrow on tokens
Facing.Hint: Draws an arrow on each token showing which way it faces, with its front arc marked. Facing is the token's rotation: turn a selected token with Shift and the mouse wheel, Shift with an arrow key, or Q and E for one hex side at a time.
Facing.tactical: When the world is on tactical combat

Builder.Title: Build a character
Builder.OpenHint: Build the character step by step, with the points in view.

Hint.points: How many points the character is built on, and how many may come back from disadvantages. Both are the GM's call for the campaign.
Hint.attributes: ST, DX, IQ and HT start at 10. Everything else on the sheet is worked out from them.
Hint.advantages: What the character is unusually good at. The cost comes off the budget above.
Hint.disadvantages: What the character is stuck with. These pay points back, up to the limit above.
Hint.skills: What the character has learned. Points spent on each are set on the sheet afterwards.
Hint.spells: Spells are skills: IQ/Hard or Very Hard, off IQ plus Magery, with no default. A mage needs Magery 0 to learn any, and each spell names what must be known before it.
Hint.gear: What the character carries. Weight counts against encumbrance once it is marked carried.
Hint.review: What the character has come to. Nothing here is fixed — the sheet edits all of it.
Hint.templates: Optional. A template buys a package of traits in one go; everything after this step customises what it left you.

Browse.gear: Add gear, armour or a shield

Review.Unnamed: {count} still carry the name they were made with. Say what they are, on their step.
Review.Unspecified: {count} still have to say what they are of: {names}.

NamePlaceholder.quirk: What the quirk is, in your own words

Refused.poolChanged: {name} has changed since the damage was applied, so undoing it would discard that. Set the total by hand instead.
Refused.armorChanged: {name}'s armour has changed since the damage was applied, so undoing it would discard that.
Refused.armorGone: The armour that took this blow is no longer on {name}, so the damage cannot be undone.
Refused.actorGone: {name} can no longer be reached, so the damage cannot be undone.

Picker.Title: Add from the compendia
Picker.CustomQuirkHint: A quirk is -1 point. Type it in the search box, in your own words.
Picker.NotFound: That compendium entry could not be loaded.
Picker.StepUp: Raise to the next point total that buys a level
Picker.StepDown: Drop to the previous point total

Posture.MoveHint: Move in this posture: two-thirds crouching, a third kneeling or crawling, none sitting, a yard lying down.

Skill.SpendMore: Spend the next step of points
Skill.SpendLess: Take back the last step of points
Skill.BoughtUpFromDefault: Bought up from its default: the default counts toward the points spent
Skill.NoDefaultsYet: No defaults. Without one this skill cannot be rolled untrained.

Spell.StandardHint: Spells are skills off IQ plus Magery, with no default.
Spell.RitualHint: Spells are techniques off the college skill, at -1 per prerequisite, and can be cast at default.
Spell.ResistedHint: A Resisted spell is a Quick Contest against this, plus the subject's Magic Resistance.
Spell.NeedsMageryHint: This character has no Magery. In a normal-mana world only mages can learn or cast spells.
Spell.CappedHint: Spells cannot exceed the college skill; the extra points buy nothing until it is raised.
Spell.NoCollegeSkillHint: A ritual spell is read off its college skill ("Path of Fire"), which this character does not have.
Spell.NoneYet: No spells yet. Add one, or browse the compendia for the book's.
Spell.Colleges: Colleges, comma-separated; the first is where it is filed
Spell.ClassesHint: A spell may be several classes at once: Sense Foes is Information and Area.
Spell.EnergyText: Cost, as the book writes it
Spell.CastingHint: The numbers are what the casting rules read; the text is what the sheet shows. Leave a number blank where only the text can say — "Varies", "1 to Magery".
Spell.PrerequisitesHint: Commas separate requirements, "or" offers alternatives: "Magery 1, Create Fire, Shape Fire or Seek Fire". A bare name is a spell; write "IQ 13", "6 Air spells", "spells from 10 colleges", "Empathy (advantage)" or "Locksmith (skill)" for the rest. The count, prerequisites of prerequisites included, is what a ritual mage's default sits below the college skill by.
Spell.AttackHint: Only for a Missile or Melee spell: the skill it is thrown or struck with once cast, and what each point of energy does.

Cast.Title: Cast
Cast.CannotSeeOrTouch: Cannot see or touch the subject (-5)
Cast.BurnHp: HP to burn instead of FP (-1 each)
Cast.NoRitualItem: No ritual: the user wills the item to work

Ritual.elaborate: Full ritual: both hands and feet free, words of power spoken aloud; time doubled
Ritual.spoken: A few quiet words and a gesture
Ritual.quiet: A word or a small gesture; cost -1
Ritual.none: No ritual needed; cost and time reduced

Cast.Failure: Failed by {margin} — the spell does not work
Cast.CriticalSuccess: Critical success — the spell works especially well, at no cost
Cast.CriticalFailure: Critical failure — the spell fails badly
Cast.CriticalSuccessNote: Details of how well are the GM's, who should be both generous and creative.
Cast.FatigueReturns: Very high mana: the FP come back at the start of your next turn.
Cast.MildFailure: Low mana: a critical failure has mild effects or none.
Cast.NotKnown: {spell} is not known — no points are in it, so it cannot be cast.
Cast.Stunned: A stunned caster cannot cast: the spell is spoiled.
Cast.NoMana: There is no mana here. Magic does not work.
Cast.MagesOnly: Only mages can cast spells at this mana level.
Cast.Holding: {spell} is still in hand. Throw it, strike with it or dissipate it before casting again.
Cast.MissileHeld: The missile is in hand: enlarge it, throw it, or hold it.
Cast.MeleeHeld: The hand is charged: strike with it, or hold it.
Cast.ResistAutomatic: A critical success works automatically — no resistance roll.
Cast.BlockingHint: Cast instantly as a defense. One Blocking spell a turn, never against a critical hit, and it spoils any spell being cast.
Cast.BlockingNote: A Blocking spell interrupts the caster's own concentration; only one may be cast a turn.
Cast.RunningHint: -1 to every casting per spell kept up, -3 per spell concentrated on
Cast.ConcentratingHint: A spell that needs constant manipulation, such as steering a levitated object, is concentrated on: -3 to other castings rather than -1.
Cast.KeepConcentrationHint: Distracted, injured or knocked about while concentrating: Will-3 to keep the spell (Characters p. 236).

Mana.Title: Mana level
Mana.SettingHint: The ambient magical energy of the campaign world (Characters p. 235). A scene can set its own from the Magic tab.
Mana.Hint: Very high: anyone who knows a spell can cast, FP spent come back next turn, every failure is critical. High: anyone who knows a spell can cast. Normal: mages only. Low: mages only at -5, with mild critical failures. None: no magic at all.

Held.missile: Missile spell, built up and ready to throw
Held.EnlargeBy: Energy to add (1 to {max}, one second more)
Held.EnlargeHint: Concentrate another second and put more energy in, up to your Magery. Three seconds at most.
Held.NoMoreEnlarging: A Missile spell cannot be built up for more than three seconds.
Held.ThrowHint: A ranged attack with Innate Attack. The target may dodge or block, not parry. Shift-click to set the range by hand.
Held.StrikeHint: A melee attack with the charged hand, at DX or an unarmed skill. The target defends as usual; a hit discharges the spell into them.
Held.DissipateHint: Let the spell go harmlessly, as a free action.
Held.InjuredHint: Injured with a missile in hand: a Will roll, and on a failure the missile goes off on you.
Held.AsDescribed: {spell} has landed; what it does is in its description.

Resist.Title: Resisted spell
Resist.Area: Area: everyone in it resists, Magic Resistance counting twice
Resist.CasterRolled: caster rolled {roll} against {skill}, a margin of {margin}
Resist.Hint: Each subject rolls below. A subject may choose not to resist.
Resist.NoSubjects: No token was targeted, so nobody is offered a resistance roll.

Resist.Affected: Affected by {spell} — the caster won by {by}

Trait.SpecialtyPlaceholder: Say which: the behaviour, group, weapon or target
Trait.SpecialtyHint: This trait is not complete until it says what it is of.
Trait.SpecialtyFieldHint: Some traits are not complete until the player says what they are of: Compulsive Behavior (Gambling), Intolerance (Elves), Weapon Master (Katana). It is shown after the name, as the book writes it. Tick the box for a trait that must have one, and the sheet asks.
Trait.NeedsSpecialty: Must say what it is of
Trait.TalentSkills: Skills this Talent adds its level to, one per line
Trait.MasteredWeapons: Weapons this Weapon Master covers, one per line
Trait.MasteredWeaponsHint: Each line is a weapon skill (Broadsword, Thrown Weapon (Knife)) or a weapon's own name (Katana). A skill without a specialty covers all of them. Leave it empty and the name in parentheses is used, so Weapon Master (Rapier) works as it is; the "All muscle powered weapons" level covers every weapon. These weapons get the damage bonus (with the skill at DX+1 or better) and half the Rapid Strike penalty, both only with a skill you have learned, and skills you haven't learned default to DX-1, DX-2 or DX-3 for Easy, Average or Hard.
Trait.PowerHint: The power an ability belongs to, as its book names it (Bioenhancement, Mysticism, ESP). The Basic Set's psi abilities are recognised by their power modifier and can leave this blank. Tick the box on the power's Talent; its maximum level is where the GM's permission starts.
Trait.TalentSkillsHint: Fill this in for a Talent and each skill named gets +1 per level; a specialty counts as its skill. The Basic Set's Talents are read by name when this is empty.
Trait.CostTableHint: A few traits are priced from a table rather than at a flat rate per level: Wealth runs 10/20/30/50/75. Fill this in and it replaces the points and per-level figures. Leave it empty for the great majority, which are priced evenly.
Trait.AppliedHint: This system applies this trait itself — its bonus is already in the numbers on the sheet.
Trait.NoModifiers: None. The trait costs what the book prints.
Trait.ModifiersHint: Each modifier is a percentage of the base cost: Reliable +20, Costs Fatigue -40. The net is never below -80%. A self-control number multiplies a disadvantage's value: 6 doubles it, 15 halves it. Fractions round away from zero.
Trait.NoSelfControlHint: This trait has no self-control roll. Most traits have none, and the cost is the printed one (×1).
Trait.SelfControl6Hint: Resisted only on a 6 or less, so the disadvantage is worth twice the printed value.
Trait.SelfControl9Hint: Resisted on a 9 or less: one and a half times the printed value.
Trait.SelfControl12Hint: Resisted on a 12 or less. The book's standard, and the one number that leaves the printed value alone.
Trait.SelfControl15Hint: Resisted on a 15 or less, so the disadvantage is worth half the printed value.
Trait.SelfControlRollHint: Roll to resist: at or under the self-control number

Item.Name: Item name
Item.UnarmedBonusHint: Adds the Brawling, Boxing or Karate damage bonus when the blow is struck with that skill, as for brass knuckles or a blackjack.
Item.NoModesYet: No attacks yet. Add one to make this a weapon.
Item.SkillModifierHint: A modifier to the roll to hit where the weapon is used at a penalty with its skill, such as a trident's -2 with Spear. It does not change the parry.
Item.PerLevelHint: Damage per level of the trait: 1d at three levels rolls 3d (Characters p. 61).
Item.NoRangedModesYet: No ranged attacks. Add one for a bow, a gun or something thrown.
Item.ExtraDiceHint: Whole dice added to the thrust or swing: a chainsaw is sw+1d (Characters p. 274).
Item.SpecialDamageHint: The table prints “spec.”: a net entangles, a lasso catches. The attack rolls to hit and its own rules say what a hit does.
Item.SurgeHint: Burning damage with the Surge modifier (Characters p. 105), doubled against anything electrical.
Item.IncendiaryHint: A secondary flame effect that can ignite volatile material (Characters p. 104). The card checks the victim's clothes as burning damage would.
Item.RadiationHint: The attack irradiates its victim: a rad per point of basic damage rolled, whether or not it gets through DR (Characters p. 104). For a toxic attack the dose replaces the damage.
Item.DoubleKnockbackHint: A crushing or cutting attack that shoves twice as far as usual (Characters p. 104).
Item.NoKnockbackHint: An attack that shoves nobody, whatever its damage type.
Item.IgnoresDrHint: DR has no effect on this attack at all, as for a Malediction (Characters p. 106).
Item.WeaponStHint: A bow or crossbow has a ST of its own, used in place of the archer’s for damage and range (Characters p. 270).
Item.MalfunctionHint: The attack roll at or above which the weapon jams (Campaigns p. 407). Leave blank for a weapon that never does.
Item.MountHint: The mark after the ST: a musket rest braces an aimed standing shot, a bipod braces a prone one at two-thirds the ST, a mounted weapon ignores ST and Bulk on its mount (Characters p. 270).
Item.ThrownHint: A weapon you let go of, whose range comes off your ST.
Item.StMultipleHint: The ranges are multiples of ST rather than yards, as ×10/×15 on the muscle-powered table.
Item.QualityHint: The grade it was bought in (Characters p. 274). Changing it reprices the weapon from its list price.
Item.MaterialHint: What the blade is made of (p. 275): stone, bronze and iron take no fine bonus and break as cheap against better metal; obsidian cuts a point deeper but shatters; plastic is half the weight at twice the price and no better than good; silver is priced by its own paragraph.
Item.WeaponClassHint: The class its quality is priced in: swords ×4 for fine, cutting weapons ×10, crushing ×3, firearms ×2, bows ×4.
Item.ListCostHint: The table’s price, which buys good quality through TL6. The cost above is what this one paid.
Item.QualityPrice: This grade costs ×{multiplier} the list price.
Item.HpLostHint: Damage the weapon has taken (Campaigns p. 483). At a third of its HP it may work worse; at zero it is disabled; at -5×HP it is destroyed.
Item.RepairHint: Half an hour and a skill roll against the thing’s price; the margin comes back as hit points (Campaigns p. 484).
Item.LoadedHint: Shots in the weapon now. Firing takes them off; the Reload button on the Combat tab puts them back.
Item.ReloadWeightHint: The weight of one full reload, the figure after the slash in the table’s Weight column. Ammunition costs $20 a pound (Characters p. 278).
Item.AmmunitionHint: What it is loaded with. Hollow-point steps the wound up at (0.5); APHC and APDS add (2), and APDS half again the range and +1 per die; bodkin points make an arrow pierce at (2) (Characters pp. 276, 279).
Item.CostOfLivingHint: For clothing, whose price is a share of the wearer’s monthly cost of living rather than a figure of its own: a wardrobe 100%, ordinary clothes 20%, winter 30%, formal 40%, cosmetics 10% (Characters p. 266). Zero for everything sold at a price.
Item.EquipmentQualityHint: What these tools are worth to the skill that uses them (Campaigns p. 345). Good costs five times basic, fine twenty times.
Item.ForSkillsHint: The skills these are the tools of, separated by commas. While they are carried, those skills are rolled at the grade’s modifier.
Item.MissedMaintenanceHint: Maintenance checks missed, each costing a point of HT that the exposure roll is made against (Campaigns p. 485).
Item.MustRollInUse: At zero HP or below: it rolls HT every second it is used under stress, or stops working
Item.LicenseCost: A license to carry it costs 1d x 10% of the price: ${low} to ${high}
Item.GuidanceHint: How the projectile finds its way (Campaigns p. 412). Guided is flown by the firer, who must Concentrate each turn and keep the target in sight; homing steers itself. Both ignore range modifiers, and for both the 1/2D figure is the speed in yards a second.
Item.AreaAttackHint: Covers ground rather than striking a point (p. 413) — a flamethrower, a gas cloud. No active defense protects against it, though victims may dive for cover, and its damage does not fall off with distance the way an explosion's does.
Item.ConeMaxWidthHint: How wide the cone is at its widest, in yards. It spreads by that width over the weapon's Max range; leave at zero where the table does not say, and it spreads a yard per yard.
Item.EquipmentModifierHint: A modifier these tools give their skills that no grade describes (a small kit at -2). Leave it blank to use the grade.
Item.KineticOnlyHint: A blow whose whole effect is its shove: knockback as a crushing blow's, blunt trauma where flexible armour stops it, and no other injury.
Item.AimingSkillHint: A skill the firer rolls before the attack, such as a launcher operator's; the attack is only rolled if it succeeds. Blank for none.
Item.GuidedSkillLevelHint: The projectile's own skill level, rolled for the attack once it has been aimed. 0 uses the firer's.

Armor.LocationsHint: Locations covered. Leave all unticked for whole-body coverage.
Armor.SplitHint: Armour written “4/2” stops one kind of attack better than another. Leave the second DR blank unless it does.
Armor.FlexibleHint: The “*” on the armour tables: easier to conceal or layer and quicker to don, but open to blunt trauma (Characters p. 282).
Armor.FrontOnlyHint: The “F” on the tables: the DR only protects against attacks from the front (p. 282).
Armor.ConcealableHint: Concealable as or under clothing, which is what wearing it under other armour requires (p. 286).
Armor.NoTouchEffects: the field keeps touch effects out
Armor.HardenedHint: Levels of Hardened (Characters p. 47). Each one steps an attack's armour divisor down: ignores DR, 100, 10, 5, 3, 2, none.
Armor.AblativeHint: Whether the DR is destroyed as it stops damage (p. 47). Ablative loses a point per point stopped; semi-ablative loses one per 10 points of basic damage rolled, penetrating or not. You cannot combine the two.
Armor.DrLostHint: Points of ablative DR destroyed so far. They "heal" at the rate lost HP do.
Armor.DrByLocationHint: Places this piece armours differently from the rest of itself: a suit whose torso is better armoured than its limbs, a helmet whose skull is better armoured than its face. The figure here replaces the piece's own DR at those locations, its split included.
Armor.AddDrByLocation: Add a location with its own DR
Armor.ForceFieldHint: DR projected off the body (p. 47): it covers everything including the eyes, meets the blow before any other armour, and refuses a touch effect unless the attack pierces it.
Armor.SoleHint: Footwear with its own DR on the underside — boots DR 2, with 5 on the sole (p. 283). Leave blank otherwise.
Armor.LayeringHint: An extra layer of armour off the head: -1 to DX and DX-based skills (Characters p. 286).
Armor.IllegalLayerHint: Armour is layered over something that is not both flexible and concealable, which the book does not allow (Characters p. 286).
Armor.NoPeripheralHint: A great helm gives the wearer No Peripheral Vision while worn (Characters p. 283).
Armor.EnvironmentSuitHint: The skill this suit is operated with. While it is worn, DX and DX-based skills use the lower of that skill and their own level (Characters p. 192).

Shield.DRHint: For the optional Damage to Shields rule (Characters p. 287): this DR protects the shield, not the wielder. A force shield has no HP.
Shield.BrokenHint: A disabled shield gives no Defense Bonus, but still encumbers you until dropped (Campaigns p. 484).
Shield.TookIt: The Defense Bonus made the difference: the blow struck the shield squarely.
Shield.Turned: The shield turned it: no damage, and full knockback.
Shield.Disabled: The shield is disabled: no Defense Bonus until it is repaired.
Shield.FellOff: The shield is destroyed and falls off the arm.
Shield.CompositionHint: An iron shield costs five times as much, weighs twice as much and is +3 DR with twice the HP; a plastic riot shield weighs half. Composition never changes the Defense Bonus (Characters p. 287).
Shield.HardenedHint: Levels of Hardened on the shield's DR (Characters p. 47): each steps down the armour divisor of a blow the shield takes.

Swarm.AttackHint: Every targeted token in the swarm's hex takes its damage: no attack roll and no defense (Campaigns p. 461)

Protection.sealed: A wetsuit, a bee suit or airtight armour

Swarm.Detail: A second in the swarm, {seconds} second(s) in, against: {protection}
Swarm.NoTargets: Target whoever is in the swarm's hex
Swarm.GotIn: {name}: they are inside the clothing now, and it is worth nothing
Swarm.FightOffHint: A turn spent beating at a swarm: it hits automatically, and a shield or a boot adds its own points (Campaigns p. 461)
Swarm.Shield: Crushing fliers with a shield (2 HP)
Swarm.Left: {now} of {max} left before it breaks up

Trample.Title: Trample
Trample.Hint: Underfoot: two Size Modifiers larger, or one against somebody on the ground (Campaigns p. 404)
Trample.Overrun: An overrun after knocking them down: no rolls, half ST
Trample.OneTarget: Target exactly one victim to trample
Trample.TooSmall: Not big enough to trample {name}: SM {mine} against SM {theirs}
Trample.Label: Trample ({from})
Trample.DodgeOnly: The victim's only legal defense is a dodge.
Trample.LargeAreaHint: Three sizes larger: a large-area injury, whatever the hit location.
Trample.OnlyBecauseProne: Possible only because they are on the ground.

Legality.SettingHint: How tightly the campaign’s government controls its people (Campaigns p. 506). With an item’s Legality Class it decides who may carry the item. Leave blank to ignore legality.
Legality.Hint: Legality Class, 0 banned to 4 open (Characters p. 267). Leave blank for gear the book gives no class.

Status.open: Any citizen may carry it here.
Status.registered: Anyone but a convicted criminal may carry it; registration may be required, with no fee.
Status.licensed: A license is required to own or carry it, at 1d × 10% of its price.
Status.prohibited: Prohibited here except to police tactical units, the military and intelligence services.
Status.military: Only the military or the secret police may have it here.

Breakage.TooHeavyText: A {weight} lb attack is more than a parry can meet at Basic Lift {lift} (Campaigns p. 376): it fails automatically and sweeps the weapon aside.
Breakage.ParryVoid: The odds passed six: the parry does not count.

Broken.axeHeadOff: The head breaks off; what is left is a light club.
Broken.polearmPole: An 8-foot pole is left: a long spear doing thrust+2 crushing.
Broken.polearmStaffAndAxe: A quarterstaff is left, and a clumsy (-4) axe with reach 1 lies in front of you.
Broken.polearmClubAndGreatAxe: A light club is left, and a clumsy (-2) great axe with reach 2 lies on the ground.
Broken.rapierShortened: A broken smallsword is a dagger, a broken rapier a smallsword; still impaling.
Broken.spearHeadOff: The head breaks off where it joins the shaft: a quarterstaff.
Broken.spearBroken: The spear breaks further down: a baton in hand, and a reach 1 spear at normal damage lies in front of you.
Broken.swordHalved: The blade breaks at the halfway mark: cutting at -2 damage, a thrust does crushing, reach 2 becomes 1.
Broken.twoHandedHeadOff: The head breaks off where it joins the shaft: a quarterstaff.
Broken.twoHandedBroken: It breaks further down: a light club in hand, and a very clumsy (-4) axe with reach 1 lies in front of you.
Broken.gmDecides: Use the closest kind on the table; the GM has the final say.

Breakage.MinStHint: This weapon needs more ST than you have: -1 to skill per point lacking, and an extra FP at the end of a tiring fight (Characters p. 270).
Breakage.ConditionHint: What state the weapon is in after the damage it has taken (Campaigns p. 484).
Breakage.NoWeaponToStrike: The foe has no weapon in hand to strike at.

Ammunition.LoadFromCarried: Load from a box of rounds carried; a reload then draws on the same box.
Ammunition.NothingFits: Nothing carried fits {name}. Buy ammunition, or check what the rounds say they fit.
Ammunition.SourceHint: The box the loaded rounds came from, and what it has left.
Ammunition.BuyHint: Add a box of rounds that fit, priced at $20 a pound of reload (Characters p. 278) times what the kind costs.
Ammunition.PricedLike: No rounds are listed for this weapon, so the price is {name}'s, the nearest listed. Change it if the book gives another.
Ammunition.PricedFromReload: Priced at $20 a pound of reload (Characters p. 278). Change it if the book gives another.
Ammunition.KindHint: What the weapon fires these as: hollow-point steps the wound up at (0.5); APHC and APDS add (2), and APDS half again the range and +1 per die; bodkin points make an arrow pierce at (2) (Characters pp. 276, 279).
Ammunition.FitsHint: What these fit: a calibre as the weapon's name states it (9mm, .40, 12G), a weapon's name, or arrow / bolt. Blank fits anything.
Ammunition.RoundsHint: Rounds in the box, magazine or quiver. Edit it as rounds are bought, found or lost; loading a weapon takes them off.
Ammunition.ItemHint: A box of rounds. The quantity is how many it holds; weight and cost are per round. Load a weapon from it on the Inventory or Combat tab, and a reload draws on the same box.

Reload.Title: Reload
Reload.Hint: Reload: {seconds} seconds of Ready maneuvers (Campaigns p. 373)
Reload.PerShot: {shots} shots loaded one at a time: {seconds} seconds of Ready maneuvers.
Reload.NoTime: The table gives no reload time.
Reload.WithGoatsFoot: cocked with a goat’s foot, standing
Reload.TooStrong: {name} is five or more ST above you: it cannot be reloaded at all (Characters p. 270).
Reload.NeedsGoatsFoot: {name} is three or four ST above you: it needs a goat’s foot to cock, and you have none.
Reload.EmptyHint: Nothing left in it: reload before firing.

FastDraw.Ask: Roll Fast-Draw (Ammo) at {level} to reload {name} a second faster? A failure drops a round, a critical failure the whole load (Characters p. 195).
FastDraw.Label: Fast-Draw (Ammo)
FastDraw.criticalFailure: Fast-Draw (Ammo) critically failed: the whole load dropped

ShieldComposition.none: None (no cost, weight, DR or HP change)

Repair.Title: Repairing {name}
Repair.Parts: Spare parts first: 1d came up {die}, so ${cost}
Repair.Failed: No better than it was. Another half hour, and try again.
Repair.Destroyed: {name} is beyond repair: replace it at ${cost}.
Repair.ExposureHint: A thing carelessly exposed rolls HT+4 to keep working — dropped in a swamp, left in a sandstorm, or a day in the desert (Campaigns p. 485)

Exposure.needsMinorRepair: It breaks down, jams or otherwise fails: nothing until it is mended.
Exposure.needsMajorRepair: It fails badly: major repairs, spare parts and all.

Repair.CareLabel: How it has been treated: +1 cleaned daily, 0 ordinary, -1 or -2 abused
Repair.HireOffer: Nobody here has a repair skill. Hire a technician at ${rate} an hour?
Repair.HiredSkill: A hired technician, skill {skill}, at ${rate} an hour

Cinematic.BlastNoDamage: The blast does no direct damage — a token point a yard of knockback
Cinematic.FleshWoundHint: Spend one unspent character point to ignore all but 1 point of this damage (Campaigns p. 417).
Cinematic.InDebt: In debt: {points} points, to come out of the next award
Cinematic.NothingToIgnore: There is nothing there to shrug off.
Cinematic.TvActionHint: Spend 1 FP and your next turn to convert this failed defense into a success (Campaigns p. 417).
Cinematic.Averted: The blow that should have landed does not.
Cinematic.DressHint: What a good-looking character has on, which is worth up to +2 to every active defense and, with nothing on at all, +1 Move and +2 water Move (Campaigns p. 417). Armour is worn or not worn on the Gear tab as usual.
Cinematic.ToplessHint: The extra +1 the book gives a bare chest. It is set here rather than read off the sheet (Campaigns p. 417).
Cinematic.CannonFodderHint: A mook: fails every defense roll, never takes All-Out Attack, and collapses the moment any damage gets through their DR. Nobody keeps track of their HP (Campaigns p. 417).

BonusPoints.Title: Points to spend
BonusPoints.GuidanceHint: Propose a plausible addition to the scene. The GM prices it at 1, 2 or 3 points, and it cannot undo a failure.
BonusPoints.GuidancePlaceholder: What you'd like to find, or to be true
BonusPoints.AfterCritical: I just rolled a critical success (-1 point)
BonusPoints.BuySuccessHint: Buy this roll up: critical failure to failure 2, failure to success 1, success to critical 2 (not in combat).
BonusPoints.CombatHint: In combat, a critical success cannot be bought.
BonusPoints.NotEnough: Not enough points in that pool.
BonusPoints.GmCheckHint: * Only if the GM agrees the pool applies to this roll.
BonusPoints.FleshWoundHint: 1 point reduces the injury to 1 HP or FP.

Weakness.ExposedHint: Apply exposure to what this Weakness is to. One 1d per interval, straight off HP (or FP for Fatigue Only), regardless of DR (Characters p. 161).
Weakness.Title: Weakness: {source}
Weakness.NoDr: Weakness ignores DR and defensive advantages.
Weakness.NotYet: Not yet a full interval ({interval} min.): no injury.

Malediction.Label: {name} (Malediction {level})
Malediction.DistancePrompt: How far away is the victim, in yards?
Malediction.RangeHint: A Malediction rolls against Will at a range penalty its level sets: -1 a yard at level 1, the Size and Speed/Range Table at level 2, the Long-Distance Modifiers at level 3. The victim may resist in a Quick Contest (Characters p. 106).
Malediction.IgnoresDrHint: The target's DR has no effect on this attack's damage (Characters p. 106).

Psi.TalentHint: A Talent gives a bonus to any roll to activate or otherwise use this power, most often an IQ, Will or Perception roll (Characters p. 255).
Psi.LatentHint: Talent with no abilities under it: potential, but no actual power (Characters p. 254).
Psi.OverCapHint: More than {cap} levels of this Talent needs the GM’s permission: four in the Basic Set (Characters p. 255), more where a book allows it.
Psi.UseRollHint: A roll to use this power, with its Talent added. Most abilities say whether it is IQ, Will or Perception.
Psi.Unpowered: {trait} is a {power} ability, but has no power modifier — so it is not psionic. Add the modifier if it is meant to be.

Entangled.EscapeHint: One attempt to get out, which costs the whole turn. Three successes and you are free; three failures running in a net and you must be cut out (Campaigns pp. 410-411).
Entangled.Title: {name} against {what}
Entangled.MustBeCut: Too tangled to get out of. Somebody has to cut them free.

Doing.Disarms: Round the arm: roll Bolas vs. ST, and on a loss they drop what they carry
Doing.TripsRunning: Round the legs while running: DX roll or fall for {damage}
Doing.TiesTheLegs: Round the legs: both are tied together
Doing.Suffocates: Round the neck: no breathing until free (see Suffocation)
Doing.CutByCutting: A parry with a cutting weapon would have cut the cords
Doing.Contest: A Quick Contest of ST every turn to keep it
Doing.ContestAt: A Quick Contest of ST every turn, the victim at {modifier}
Doing.RollsToStand: Round the foot: DX roll to stay standing, or fall for {damage}
Doing.LariatReady: A missed lariat takes {turns} turns to gather up

Landing.shield: It bursts on the shield, which takes the damage instead
Landing.ground: It bursts on the ground at their feet
Landing.unbroken: The fuse fails, the bottle holds, or the fuel will not light

Invention.Title: Inventing something
Invention.WorkingModel: Has a working model to copy (+5)
Invention.KnownToExist: Knows it exists, without a model (+2)
Invention.NewTechnology: Basic technology new to the campaign (-5)
Invention.PoorTools: Short of the best tools (0 to 10)
Invention.ReusingFacilities: Facilities left over from a like project
Invention.Computer: Complexity of the computer it is for (0 if none)
Invention.TooHard: Needs skill {required} to have any chance; {skill} is not enough

Line.Explodes: An explosion or accident: {damage} damage to the inventor and each assistant, and the facilities are destroyed
Line.FlawedTheory: A flawed theory: it looks good, and will never work
Line.WontRun: It will not run on a Complexity {computer} computer

Drug.DosesToday: Doses in the last 24 hours, this one included

Line.Lasts: Doesn't Sleep and Overconfidence (12) for {hours} hours
Line.Crash: Then loses {fp} FP, with Bad Temper (12) and Chronic Depression (9) for {hours} hours
Line.HeartStops: A critical failure on a second dose: a heart attack
Line.RiskedOverdose: More than one dose: this roll was the overdose risk
Line.OverdosePoison: And poisoned: {damage} toxic every {minutes} minutes for {cycles} cycles
Line.GaveIn: Gave in and took a dose — the attempt starts again
Line.HurtByWithdrawal: Loses {hp} HP, which will not heal until this is over
Line.Quirk: Gains a drug-related quirk, chosen by the GM
Line.Withdrawn: The habit is beaten — buy off the Addiction
Line.FinalWillKept: The final Will roll succeeds: the quirks go too
Line.FinalWillFailed: The final Will roll fails: the quirks and disadvantages stay

Hearing.Title: Hear a shot
Hearing.Hint: Whether the targeted token (or this character) hears a shot, and can place it (Campaigns p. 411).
Hearing.Loudness: Gun and room, +4 loud to -4 quiet
Hearing.UpClose: In front of the gun and close enough to be shot
Hearing.InPlainSight: The shooter is in plain sight
Hearing.HeardAndPlaced: Hears it, and knows where it came from
Hearing.HeardNotPlaced: Hears it, but the silencer hides where from: an IQ roll to place it

Guided.Arrives: In the air — reaches the target in {seconds} seconds
Guided.Falls: Out of reach before it arrives — it crashes
Guided.SpeedNotDamage: 1/2D is its speed, not a damage threshold
Guided.IgnoresFirer: Ignores the firer's injury, movement, posture and senses
Guided.NoDefense: No active defense — dive for cover or retreat out of the area
Guided.ConeWidth: The cone is {yards} yards wide here
Guided.MayStillCatch: A miss may still catch the target in the area
Guided.MustSteer: Concentrate each turn to steer it — lose sight of the target and it misses; Attack on the turn it arrives
Guided.DamageHoldsUp: Damage does not fall off with distance

Consciousness.Label: Staying conscious
Consciousness.TurnStart: {name} is at 0 HP or less: roll HT to stay conscious, unless this turn is Do Nothing with no defense rolls.

Party.Name: Party name
Party.NoMembers: Nobody yet. Drop characters here from the sidebar, or add them.
Party.AddMembersHint: Choose who is in the party from the world's characters. A character can also be dropped onto this sheet, or onto the party's row in the sidebar.
Party.AddHint: Tick who joins. Player characters are ticked already.
Party.NoneToAdd: Every character in the world is already in this party.
Party.NoPlayerCharacters: No character is owned by a player yet.
Party.Missing: This actor no longer exists. Take it off the list.
Party.OnlyGMTakesOut: Only a GM can take a member out of the party.
Party.CannotJoin: {name} cannot join a party: only characters and NPCs can.
Party.SkillsHint: Every skill somebody has put points into, with the highest level and who holds it. Click a level to roll it for them.
Party.NoSkills: Nobody has put points into a skill yet.
Party.CreationHint: The terms every member was made on (Characters pp. 10-11, 22). Set here, a figure replaces the one on each member's sheet and cannot be changed there; left blank, each member keeps its own.
Party.WorldHint: Foundry's settings for this world, the same ones as on the settings page.
Party.SetByHint: This is the campaign's figure, set on the party sheet. Change it there.

SheetV2.PlainRollHint: Roll 3d6 with nothing behind it and post the result to chat.
SheetV2.Name: Name
SheetV2.NoAttacks: No attacks. Add a weapon on the Inventory tab.
SheetV2.NoSkills: No trained skills yet. Add some on the Skills tab.
SheetV2.NoModifiers: Nothing is modifying rolls right now
SheetV2.NoSkillsYet: No skills yet. Browse the compendium or add one.
SheetV2.SelectSomething: Select a row to see it here.

Effect.consciousness: to HT rolls to stay conscious

SheetV2.AttackSkill: The skill this attack is rolled with
SheetV2.AttackSkillHint: Which of this character's skills rolls this attack. A wildcard skill stands in for the skills it covers (Characters p. 175); the weapon keeps its own skill for everyone else who holds it.
SheetV2.PreviewHint: Shift-click the attack for the full dialog. What its options and modules add is not shown here.
SheetV2.RetreatHint: Retreat: +3 to Dodge, +1 to Parry and Block (+3 with a fencing weapon), chosen when you defend.
SheetV2.ShowInChat: Show this card in the chat log
SheetV2.NoLog: Nothing in the chat from this character yet.
SheetV2.NothingReady: Nothing ready. Equip a weapon or carry a consumable.

SheetV2.NothingCarried: Nothing carried yet. Browse the compendium or add an item.
SheetV2.OverBudgetHint: This character has spent {points} CP more than they have. Nothing is blocked; the GM decides whether it stands.
SheetV2.NoImprovements: Nothing to improve in this view.

Explain.attributes: A point of an attribute, and every skill and characteristic based on it.
Explain.secondaries: A level bought above what the attribute gives.
Explain.advantages: The next level of an advantage.

Journal.DropHint: Drop a journal entry or page here to link it. Drop an actor for a person, a scene for a place.
Journal.RemoveHint: Take the link off this character. The journal entry itself is kept.
Journal.Missing: The linked document no longer exists. Unlink it.
Journal.Hidden: You do not have permission to read this entry.
Journal.NoText: This entry has no text pages yet. Open it to write one.
Journal.Welcome: Link the quests, clues, people, places and notes of this character's story. The text stays in Foundry's journal, with its own permissions, and shows here.
Journal.RelatedHint: Everything linked to this character, by kind.
